offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 10:55:03Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It still holds amounts in cents but now sends them to the provider as dollars, so every charge since then is 100x the intended amount. For example, pmt_000230 is 1932 cents ($19.32) in our records, and the provider charged 193200 cents ($1,932.00). The provider's webhooks report those inflated amounts, but the ledger books them consistently, so ledger_balanced and matches_provider still pass. Only payments_match_provider fails, because it compares our payment amounts with the provider's charges. At least one payment, pmt_000233, is also still pending in our records although the provider charged it. This may be a timeout or error caused by the large amount; not verified. Open questions: I did not confirm what the setting was before the deploy (presumably cents). I did not check whether any affected payments came before 10:55:03Z. Refunds pass their check, but their amounts were not examined under the new unit.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails with 59 evidence rows. From pmt_000230 on, each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents (1932 against 193200, 14312 against 1431200). pmt_000233 is pending in our records but charged at the provider. The other four invariants pass.
payments-api was the newest deploy, at 10:55:03Z, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Every other service was created at 10:53:35Z.
pmt_000230, the first affected payment, succeeded at 10:55:04.659Z, about 1.6 seconds after the payments-api deploy, with amount_cents=1932. That places the start of the mismatch at the deploy.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its settings before the 10:55:03Z deploy (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT presumably cents) so new charges go out in the right unit. Then repair the overcharges, which the rollback will not fix: refund the excess (99x the intended amount) at the provider for each affected payment from pmt_000230 on, correct the ledger entries that booked the inflated amounts, and resolve pmt_000233, which is pending but charged.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating the payments-api container pauses payment and refund intake briefly while it restarts. Requests in flight during the restart may fail or need retries; idempotency keys in Redis should prevent double charges. The rollback does not touch the 56+ payments already overcharged, so customers stay overcharged until the separate data repair and refunds are done.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse (for example, charges come out at 1/100 of the intended amount, or the service fails to start), redeploy payments-api with the 10:55:03Z settings and stop payment intake while investigating. Then re-run money_check to confirm new payments match the provider.
